# Challenge: your publication-ready volcano

This is the hands-on hour. You've built every piece — now make a volcano plot you'd be
proud to put in a paper. **Use your AI assistant freely.**

**Your mission:** start from `de_plot` and produce a polished volcano that:

1. shows dashed threshold lines (fold change ±1, p = 0.05);
2. **labels the ~10 most significant genes** (hint: the `ggrepel` package);
3. has a clean theme, a clear title, and readable, colourblind-friendly colours;
4. is one you can explain to a colleague in a sentence.

Everything you need is already loaded: `de_plot`, `volcano`, and the `tidyverse`.

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Remember the big idea:</strong> the plot is the answer to
  <em>"which genes change between biofilm and planktonic?"</em> — make that answer
  jump out.
</div>

> 🤖 **Ask your AI** (ideas): *"How do I label only the top 10 genes on a ggplot volcano
> with ggrepel?"* · *"Suggest a colourblind-friendly palette for up/down/ns."* ·
> *"How do I make this figure look publication-ready?"* — then **run it, read it, and
> check it does what you expect.**

<details>
<summary>One possible solution</summary>
```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ggrepel)

top_genes <- de_plot %>%
  filter(status != "Not significant") %>%
  slice_max(-log10(padj), n = 10)

ggplot(de_plot, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj))) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = status), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, aes(label = gene_id),
                  size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Up in biofilm"   = "#D55E00",
                                 "Down in biofilm" = "#0072B2",
                                 "Not significant" = "grey70")) +
  labs(title = "S. aureus: biofilm vs planktonic (24 h)",
       x = "log2 fold change", y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```
</details>

## Showcase {-}

Share your figure with the room — what's your favourite gene, and what does it tell you
about how *S. aureus* lives in a biofilm? 🎉

### Going further {-}

If you finish early: label genes by **name** instead of ID, make the plot
**interactive** with `ggplotly()`, or try a **heatmap** of your top genes across all
samples.
